topic: Error Correction and Hamming Codes: The Self-Healing Data
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Electrical Engineering)

sections.title: The Problem: The Noisy Universe
lecture_lines: Radiation can flip bits during data transmission.
A single bit flip changes the message meaning.
Without checks, the receiver cannot detect errors.
This corruption causes systems to behave unexpectedly.
Hamming codes detect and fix these silent errors.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Simple Parity Bit
lecture_lines: Parity bits detect if an error occurred.
Even parity makes the total count of ones even.
However, it cannot locate or fix the error.
animations: Show binary "101" (#FFFFFF); a green '0' (#00FF00) appears at the end with the label "Parity" (#00FF00). Change Line 1 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Sum the '1's; a box highlights the two '1's and parity '0'. Show math "1+1+0=2 (Even)" (#FFFFFF). Change Line 2 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Flip a bit to '1'; the entire block turns red (#FF0000) indicating error. Label "ODD - ERROR!" (#FF0000) appears. Change Line 3 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).

sections.title: The Hamming Logic: Overlapping Circles
lecture_lines: Richard Hamming used overlapping circles for data.
Data bits sit in the intersections of these circles.
Each circle is managed by a specific parity bit.
Flipping a data bit affects multiple parity circles.
This unique intersection points directly to the error.
animations: Draw three overlapping circles in red (#FF0000), green (#00FF00), and blue (#0000FF). Change Line 1 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Place a white '1' (#FFFFFF) in the central intersection of all circles. Change Line 2 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Labels P1 (#FF0000), P2 (#00FF00), P3 (#0000FF) appear in the outer sections of each circle. Change Line 3 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
The central '1' flips to '0'; all three circles pulse orange (#FFA500). Change Line 4 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
A white arrow (#FFFFFF) points to the unique central overlap area with label "Target Bit" (#FFFFFF). Change Line 5 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).

sections.title: The Power of 2: Positioning Bits
lecture_lines: Parity bits occupy positions at powers of two.
All other positions hold the actual message data.
This specific layout enables the mathematical correction magic.
animations: Display numbers 1-7; highlight 1, 2, and 4 in blue (#5555FF) with labels "P1", "P2", "P4" (#5555FF). Change Line 1 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Fill positions 3, 5, 6, 7 with white 'D' characters (#FFFFFF) and labels "D3", "D5", "D6", "D7" (#FFFFFF). Change Line 2 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Arrange the labels into the sequence [P1, P2, D3, P4, D5, D6, D7] in a horizontal line. Change Line 3 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).

sections.title: The Calculation: Who Checks Whom?
lecture_lines: Every bit position has a unique binary address.
Parity bit 1 checks addresses ending in one.
Parity bit 2 checks addresses with a middle one.
Parity bit 4 checks addresses starting with one.
This creates a digital fingerprint for every position.
animations: List binary indices 001 to 111 vertically in white (#FFFFFF). Change Line 1 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Highlight rows with a '1' in the last digit in cyan (#00FFFF) with label "Checks P1" (#00FFFF). Change Line 2 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Highlight rows with a '1' in the middle digit in magenta (#FF00FF) with label "Checks P2" (#FF00FF). Change Line 3 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Highlight rows with a '1' in the first digit in yellow (#FFFF00) with label "Checks P4" (#FFFF00). Change Line 4 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Highlight index 011 (3) to show it's within both cyan and magenta groups. Change Line 5 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).

sections.title: Correction: Finding the 'Syndrome'
lecture_lines: Recalculate each parity bit in the received message.
Red indicators show which parity checks failed.
Sum the positions of the failing parity bits.
This sum identifies the exact error location.
Flip the identified bit to correct the data.
animations: Show the bit sequence [P1, P2, D3, P4, D5, D6, D7] in white (#FFFFFF). Highlight parity bits P1, P2, P4 as they are recalculated. Change Line 1 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
P1 and P2 turn red (#FF0000), indicating they fail their parity checks. Label "FAIL" (#FF0000) appears above them. Change Line 2 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
Display the math "1 + 2 = 3" in white text (#FFFFFF) below the sequence. Change Line 3 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).
The bit at position 3 (D3) is highlighted with a yellow box (#FFFF00) and label "ERROR BIT" (#FFFF00). Change Line 4 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).

Bit D3 flashes green (#00FF00) and flips its value. Display [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/based.svg] next to it with label "FIXED" (#00FF00). Change Line 5 color to #FFFF00. self.wait(2).

sections.title: Real-World Impact: From RAM to Deep Space
lecture_lines: Hamming codes protect modern server memory from crashes.
They allow deep-space probes to communicate reliably.
This math ensures your bank balance remains accurate.
